events.name: Black men ejected from the Musical Fund Hall gallery during the Reform Convention debate on 'white'
events.location: Musical Fund Hall, Locust Street, Philadelphia
events.description: On Saturday, Jan. 20, 1838, while the Reform Convention at Musical Fund Hall debated inserting the word 'white' into the suffrage article, Black men were ejected from the spectators' gallery. The Pennsylvania Freeman of Jan. 25, 1838 reports that four were forcibly ejected: 'John P. Burr, Thomas Butler, and James Forten, jr., with another highly respectable and worthy colored man.' Michiko Quinones identifies the fourth man as John Vashon (2026-11-03). The 1838 Black Metropolis post 'Thrown Out of Democracy' (historical fiction based on the newspapers) tells it as two planned actions. In the morning John Vashon and Lewis Woodson (the post prints 'Louis'), first in line for the gallery, were confronted by the doorkeeper Thomas Jefferson Becket and protested their right to be there. At 5 p.m. Burr, Butler and James Forten Jr. entered the gallery. Burr and Butler left when ordered out; Forten Jr. stayed seated and was dragged out by Becket and his men, and later sued Becket. The post assumes the actions were planned, and places a strategy meeting on Jan. 19 at James Forten's home at 4th and Lombard as a high-probability guess. Representative Earle argued that day for keeping the vote, waving a Black man's passport, probably Robert Purvis's. The convention voted 77 to 45 to insert 'white'.
attendees: ejected from the gallery; dragged out; later sued Becket
ejected from the gallery: the fourth man the Freeman does not name (identified by Michiko Quinones, 2026-11-03); in line for the gallery that morning, per the blog post
